title: Finance and Bursary Administrator
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join a highly regarded education and training organisation supporting the development of future professionals across the South West.

This organisation is known for its collaborative culture, commitment to personal development and supportive working environment, offering the opportunity to become part of a team that genuinely invests in its people.

Your new role

As a Finance & Bursary Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting both the financial and operational administration of a busy training programme.
You will be responsible for:
- Raising invoices and supporting day-to-day finance administration.
- Maintaining accurate financial records, spreadsheets and databases.
- Supporting funding and bursary administration processes.
- Assisting with payment schedules and reconciliations.
- Supporting trainee onboarding and record management.
- Administering trainee databases and ensuring information is maintained accurately.
- Responding to enquiries via telephone and email.
- Liaising with trainees, partner organisations and internal stakeholders.
- Supporting compliance, audit and reporting activities.
- Working closely with the Management Accountant and wider team.

This is a varied position combining finance administration, stakeholder engagement and programme support within a friendly and supportive environment.
What you'll need to succeedTo be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous finance administration, accounts administration or office administration experience.
- Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confidence maintaining accurate records and databases.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
- A positive, resilient and proactive approach.

Experience within finance, accounts payable, purchase ledger, business support, education administration or customer-focused administration would be highly advantageous, although full training will be provided on the specialist elements of the role.
What you'll get in return
- £16.75 per hour PAYE Premium or £18.93 per hour Umbrella.
- 37 hours per week.
- 33 days annual leave.
- Free onsite parking.
- Onsite café and excellent facilities.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.
- Ongoing mentoring and development.
- Exposure to a broad range of finance and administrative responsibilities.
- Initial contract expected until Christmas with the potential for extension and longer-term opportunities.

Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

title: Service Administrator
company: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
description: The post holder will support the Administration Line Managers/Service Coordinators by Co-ordinating a professional, efficient and effective administrative service to patients and visitors in accordance with Trust policies and standards The role will coordinate and organise the attendance of patients to outpatient, inpatient & day case appointments in line with local team and Trust arrangements as instructed Ensure all administrative processes; and enquiries are dealt with in an efficient and timely manner, following agreed standard operating procedures, escalating to senior manager as appropriate Undertake general clerical duties to maximise all available capacity in an appropriate way Proof reading clinical letters (please note there is no audio typing in this role) Monitoring waiting times, ensuring that our patients treatment pathways, from referral to treatment are accurate and up to date (for more information on what this means please visit - NHS England Referral to treatment) Ensure all information is secure and confidentiality of information is maintained at all times Provide excellent customer care which may include communica For more detail about the main duties of this role, please see the job description section below. As a key member of the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, you will be joining an exceptional team working together to help our patients to stay healthy, when they need it most. For more information on the Job Description and Responsibilities please click the link below. More detail about the role We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic and motivated Service Administrator to join our Trauma & Orthopaedic team in the Princess Elizabeth Orthopaedic Centre. The successful candidates must be highly motivated with excellent communication skills, enjoy working within a busy and vibrant team. They must be able to prioritise their workload and able to work well under pressure. Secretarial experience, knowledge of working in a hospital environment and medical terminology are all desirable for this role, but not essential. You will have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and proven experience in dealing with service users on the telephone. You will be flexible and adaptable with excellent IT skills. You will need to enjoy the challenge of working as part of a busy team yet have the ability to use your own initiative to meet the changing needs of the department and orthopaedic service as a whole. If you feel you would be able to meet the demands of this challenging and rewarding role, then we would be delighted to hear from you. Visits to the department are welcome and encouraged. Working Pattern: 22.5 hours Wednesday, Thursday and Fridays 09.00-17.00 Interview Date: To be confirmed For further information please contact: Jazz Rockey, Admin Line Manager on jasmin.rockey@nhs.net This is a 12 months fixed term contract . For current NHS employees this post could be a secondment opportunity. As an inclusive employer, the Royal Devon values diversity and is committed to creating a culture of inclusivity where everyone can be themselves and reach their full potential. We believe in fostering a sense of belonging and actively encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, cultures, and abilities. We recognise the advantages of having a diverse workforce that reflects the communities we serve. Preference will be given to staff with Priority and 'At Risk' status including NHS At Risk staff throughout Devon. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust reserves the right to close vacancy when sufficient applications have been received. The Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust was established in April 2022, bringing together the expertise of both the Royal Devon and Exeter NHS Foundation Trust and Northern Devon Healthcare NHS Trust. Benefits We will work together to maintain a culture that develops and supports you and your team. This might include funding for a care certificate, a degree or leadership qualifications. Or it might include days off to study, engage in CPD or rotational placements to help you hone your skills. Wherever you are heading in the NHS, we'll help you get there. Looking after you is important to us. We strive to help our staff create a healthy work-life balance through flexible working schemes and our family friendly policies. If you're starting out in the NHS, you'll start with 27 days paid annual leave (plus bank holidays), rising to 33 days plus bank holidays. You'll benefit from access to our own comprehensive occupational health services, including counselling, onsite wellbeing activities and groups. Salary is not the only financial benefit You'll have access to an extensive range of staff discounts on shopping, fitness and leisure options and you can spread the cost of technology and home appliance purchases from major retailers. You will also have access to other benefits including: National discount services such as the Blue Light Card and Health Service Discounts. Salary sacrifice options including our OFSTED rated outstanding nursery onsite at Exeter Car lease schemes. The NHS Pension scheme (one of the most generous and comprehensive in the UK). Cycle to work scheme These are just a few of the benefits available if the role is something you are interested in, we'd love to hear from you.

Join Pinhoe View as a Receptionist to be the welcoming face of our hospital and provide vital administrative support across our services. As our Receptionist, you will play an essential role in creating a professional, friendly and supportive experience for everyone who visits the hospital. Shift pattern hours - weekdays: 7:00am – 3:00pm or 12:00midday – 8:00pm and 1 in 3 weekends: 9:00am – 5:00pm. As the Receptionist, you will be: To be the first point of contact for staff and visitors at reception, answering inbound calls promptly and professionally. Transferring calls to the relevant staff or taking messages, passing these along to the relevant staff in an efficient and timely manner. Ensuring that all visitors sign in to meet the requirements of health & safety and are provided with visitors passes so they can be identified as visitors to the hospital. Ensuring that visitors leaving site have signed out so that hospital staff are aware they are no longer on site. Ensure that all keys and alarms are allocated and signed out to staff and signed back in at the end of shift/visit. Ensuring that the key management paperwork is accurately completed so that key management can be evidenced for regulatory purposes. Ensure all visitors to the Hospital read and sign the contraband item list. Complete radio response checks daily to ensure that compliance with radios are adhered to. To be successful in this role, you will be: The ability to always display professional conduct. Ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships. Ability to manage stressful situations. Demonstrated ability to always maintain confidentiality. Accuracy, efficiency, timeliness, and diligence are displayed in the accomplishment of all assigned duties with a minimum of direct supervision. Ability to prioritise duties and responsibilities. Experience using office software (emails, calendars, word and excel) (Essential) GCSE certificate, Grade C or above in English, or equivalent (Essential).
